steps.text: Whisk flour, milk, water, baking powder, and salt together in a bowl until smooth.
Heat vegetable or canola oil in a deep fryer to 365 degrees F (185 degrees C).
Pat fish fillets dry with paper towels to help ensure batter sticks; dip fish fillets into the batter to coat.
Carefully lower fillets, one at a time, into hot oil. Fry several fillets at a time without overcrowding the pan, turning once, until cooked through and golden brown, about 2 minutes per side.
Drain fried fish fillets on a wire rack over a paper-towel lined pan.

raw_recipe.headline: Unbelievable Fish Batter
raw_recipe.description: This fish batter recipe uses flour, baking powder, salt, milk, and water to create an incredibly light and crispy batter on your favorite white fish.

video.description: With a good filet of fish and a bowl full of batter, you can create a delicious, light, and crispy fish coating. All it takes is a few ingredients you probably have on hand, like: flour, milk and spices.

review.reviewBody: This is just spectacular. I had real problems with batter (soggy, tasteless, too thin etc), but this was so crisp and light! I too, cut the baking powder down to 2 tbspns, but I used self-raising flour (all I had on hand) and it worked perfectly. I had no problem with it sticking to the thing I was battering (fresh pecorino cheese cubes - it was too wonderful to contemplate!). For such a simple recipe, you'll get fabulous results - guaranteed!

We used a total of 2 T baking powder which worked very well – w/o the bitter aftertaste previous reviewers have written about. We also added ¼ tsp. Old Bay & an equal amount of LA Gold (hot sauce). 5 +++ stars from us. We’ll be making this recipe again!!!

This recipe was awesome! The fish turned out so great. I used 3/4 c of milk and 3/4 c of water because the batter was too thick at first. I added salt, pepper and garlic powder to the mixture as well. I fried the fish in 1/2 an inch of vegetable oil. Everyone raved about it!

This turned out pretty good. I did only 2T of the baking soda as the other review suggested. I also dredged the fish in flour first to help the batter stick. Either fry it up in a non stick pan or make sure your grease is deep enough to float the fish in to prevent sticking to the pan.

This is great. I used self rising flour (that I seasoned really well) instead and decreased the baking powder. And like some of the other reviews, I also increased the liquid because the batter is really thick.

This is a perfect batter. It's thick, and coats the fish nicely and yet, doesn't come out overly oily. I do spice the flour with garlic powder, italian seasoning, salt, pepper and vegetable seasoning. I followed suggestions and lowered the baking powder to 2 tbsp. It's a good batter for pretty much anything going in the fryer. Cheese, onion rings etc. (Try the cheese, it's phenomenal!)

This was just terrific. I always struggle with frying fish in the typical bread crumb coating, and this solved the dilemma forever! I too reduced the baking powder to 2T, but did not change anything else. The coating is a little messy to apply, but wasn't a problem. It can be thicker or thinner to your taste. Absolutely delcious! It reminded my family of the old Arthur Treacher's fried fish (or Long John Silver's). Thank you!!!

This is a good basic recipe. Nice crispiness! I used 3/4 cup of flour instead of half a cup, and only 2T of baking powder. I also added 1T onion powder, garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon of white pepper, and 1T crab seafood seasoning. Dredged in flour then dipped in batter. This was a perfect batter. I also used it to deep fry red and yellow bell peppers.

They made a mistake it is suppose to be 1Tbl spoon of baking powder. Also i added 4 table spoons of corn starch. Makes it extra crispy and tender inside. Along with onion ,garlic powder 1tbls of each and i used black pepper,salt 1Tspn. Patted the fish dry .rolled in some flour and dipped it in the batter. Shook off and extra and fried 5min on each side. Then put on wire rack not paper towels. They hold the grease in. Also use wesson oil. I find it works the best. Good eating everyone.

Absolutely fantastic! Used it to coat my cod filets. For the most part I followed the recipe to a T. I made a couple minor adjustments in seasoning/taste. I added 1 tsp of sugar, 1/2 tsp black pepper, and an additional 1/2 tsp salt because I didn’t feel like seasoning the fish itself, I was being lazy lol. I added sugar because I find that a lot of batters have just the slightest hint of sweetness to it. This is how I used it: I used about 2 lbs of thawed cod filets, which I broke in half to make for faster and easier frying. I heated vegetable oil (about 1-2 inches deep) in a high sided fry pan on medium high heat. I patted the fish dry. I dropped a blob of batter into the oil to check for temperature and when it started bubbling and frying, I then decided to start cooking the fish. I cooked the fish by batches of 4 to 6 pieces at a time so as not to clutter the pan and bring down the heat. I battered the fish as I cooked them, not all before hand. I cooked the fish for about 4 minutes on each side, and for longer on thicker pieces. I drained on a plate with paper towel. Honestly this was some of the best fried fish I’ve ever had. Super easy and definitely worth a try!! Even the 5 year old exclaimed (more than once) at how yummy the fish was.

So light and crispy. The batter was a little thick so I thinned it with a bit of water. I added just a squeeze of fresh lemon juice. I patted dry the fish fillets and then dredged them with a seasoned flour mixture. The batter didn't separate from the fish. Will use this again. EXCELLENT!!

This made the perfect amount of batter for a full pack of fish. I added lemon pepper seasoning to the mix... I didn't quite add enough, but there was enough to where you could barely taste it. Either way i'm saving this one!
Yumm. Better than bought at a shop

This was terrible. I typically trust every All Recipe, so I hadn't read the reviews before I tried it. Needless to say, two TABLEspoons is way too much baking powder. We actually couldnt eat it. And I see it was reduced from 1/4 cup! I can only imagine the taste then.

I made it with self rising flour instead of all purpose, seasoned it with seasoned salt and added a little corn starch. Tasted great but didn't brown in the air fryer. So if you going to air fry this is not for you.
Batter wouldn’t stick when frying stuck to the bottom of the pan and fell off my fish

This is one of the most awful thing I've ever eaten in this decade. Upon further inspection(I have little knowledge of cooking). You're supposed to use 2 TEASPOONS(probably even less). NOT 2 tablespoons. This recipe resulted in the most bitter meal you could possibly imagine.
I made one half of the recipe. Reduced the flour by one tablespoon which I substituted for one tablespoon of cornstarch. The fish was amazing!!

Lives up to the name for sure. We made this for Good Friday and everyone was raving about it! So light and crispy! I only added salt as we were serving it with homemade tarter sauce and seasoned fries. 10/10

This batter was absolutely amazing!!!! I used pieces of fresh cod sprinkled with Old Bay and a little salt. I deep fried them. The first one stuck to the bottom but came up easily. For the second piece, I held it in the oil a bit before letting it go and it fried perfectly!! Definitely a keeper recipe !
